correctness.rationale: Starting from the exact finite-speed rest-state generator, the derived three moment equations imply strict M monotonicity and the exact Eq. (16) Laplace ODE. Its leading rational coefficients are P=(1+theta)/s+O(1) and Q=-C/s^3+O(s^-2); integrating factors give F~[C/(1-theta)]s^-2 subcritically and F~C s^-2 log(1/s) at theta=1. Positive monotonic M satisfies a standard Laplace Tauberian theorem. Exact symbolic residues and two independent parameter-family ODE integrations passed; numerical samples are not used as infinite-time proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed advance is a quantitatively exact equality-case logarithmic law and the finite-rate subcritical coefficient; the already published model, parameter boundary, and Laplace moment equation are not claimed as new. The closest classical elephant-walk law is acknowledged as a genuine close analogy, but it is a distinct discrete-time process without the finite-speed and positive exponential resting-time parameters. Explicit same-paper full-text comparison and targeted published-record searches found no exact statement of this finite-rate critical amplitude. Residual implicit coverage remains a publication-priority risk.
residual_risks: The primary full text already contains the exact transform equation; the asserted conclusion could be viewed as an implicit result or modest refinement rather than an independent discovery.
The discrete elephant walk has the same critical logarithmic universality class; an unlocated general theorem for finite-state run/rest embeddings could imply the result.
No independent publication-priority or external scientific audit has been undertaken.

value.rationale: The equality surface between finite-diffusivity and power-law superdiffusion in a motivated positive-rate run/rest transport model is neither an arbitrary parameter slice nor mere extrapolation: finite-speed moment dynamics produce a new marginal t log t law with a physical rate-dependent amplitude. The finite-diffusion coefficient is exact, and divergence toward the phase surface shows an observable, nonanalytic transport boundary. Established elephant-walk universality and the narrowness of this refinement are included as value risks.
